findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_upload" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Mint a single-use upload URL for pushing a conversation-attached PDF to Bankstatemently before converting it. Use this ONLY when you have no other way to refere…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement · Private data: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement, categorize_statement, dismiss_statement, get_credits, rate_statement, list_transactions · Public sink: request_upload, get_statement, get_credits, rate_statement · Destructive: categorize_statement, dismiss_statement.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement · Private data: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement, categorize_statement, dismiss_statement, get_credits, rate_statement, list_transactions · Public sink: request_upload, get_statement, get_credits, rate_statement · Destructive: categorize_statement, dismiss_statement

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
